questions.question: For interval scheduling (maximum number of non-overlapping meetings), which greedy rule is optimal?
questions.explanation: Choosing the meeting that ends first leaves the most room for the rest; an exchange argument shows swapping it into any optimal solution never makes it worse.

questions.question: With coins [1, 3, 4], what does largest-coin-first greedy return for amount 6?
options: [4, 1, 1] — not optimal, since [3, 3] uses fewer coins
questions.explanation: Greedy takes 4 then 1 and 1 (three coins), but 3 + 3 needs only two. Minimum-coin change for arbitrary denominations needs DP.

questions.question: What is the standard technique for proving a greedy algorithm correct?
options: Testing it on a few examples
Showing it runs in O(n log n)
The exchange argument: swap an optimal solution's choice for the greedy choice without making it worse
questions.explanation: The exchange argument transforms any optimal solution step by step into the greedy one while preserving optimality.

questions.question: Why is greedy by value-per-kg optimal for fractional knapsack but not for 0/1 knapsack?
options: Fractional knapsack always has fewer items
Splitting lets you always fill leftover capacity with the next-best ratio; with whole items, leftover space can be wasted
Greedy is actually optimal for both
questions.explanation: When items can be split, the best ratio always fills capacity exactly. With whole items only, an early high-ratio pick can leave unusable space, so DP is required.
